hypotheses.description: OpsFlow Enterprise Lite (13 modules, 40 requirements) too small for multi-agent benefit
hypotheses.name: Benchmark Size
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Run same benchmark at 2x scale (26 modules, 80 requirements) to see if Vanilla degrades
evidenceAgainst: 7 agents still completed the project to 80% of Vanilla quality
Worker isolation did prevent scope contamination
evidenceFor: Vanilla handled 40 endpoints, 15 tables, 5 services cleanly in one pass
No context pressure symptoms in Vanilla run (no truncation, no simplification)
13 modules is below typical multi-agent threshold (20+ modules)
AGENT-5 complexity floors (80 files, 300 exports) were low enough for single agent

hypotheses.description: 7-agent orchestration overhead consumed any potential quality gain
hypotheses.name: Agent Overhead
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Test with 3 agents (1 builder + reviewer + verifier) instead of 7
evidenceAgainst: Gatekeepers caught real issues (endpoint gaps, module coverage)
Evidence quality gains were real and measurable
evidenceFor: 3-4x process overhead vs Vanilla baseline
3 gatekeeper agents added review/verification time without implementation contribution
Handoff/receipt/capsule generation added artifact burden
Spawn coordination added serialization overhead

hypotheses.description: Orchestrator did not enforce AGENT-5 complexity floors during implementation
hypotheses.name: Orchestrator Failure
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Add hard floor enforcement to orchestrator: block closure if floors unmet
evidenceAgainst: Orchestrator did spawn 4 builders with correct fork_context:false
Orchestrator did not write worker scope
evidenceFor: v0.5 missed export floor (185/300) and endpoint floor (35/40)
Orchestrator allowed AGENT-8 to close with PASS_WITH_CAVEAT despite 11/13 modules
No mid-run floor enforcement mechanism existed

hypotheses.description: Reviewer gate was too permissive; closure gate did not block on caveats
hypotheses.name: Integration/Reviewer Failure
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Make reviewer caveats blocking (P0) for phase closure
evidenceAgainst: Reviewer was READONLY, correctly identified issues
evidenceFor: Reviewer flagged 11/13 modules, 36/40 endpoints, 16/30 error codes as caveats
Phase still closed with PASS despite these gaps
No mechanism to force repair before closure

hypotheses.description: Worker scope division (DB/Backend/Frontend/Tests) created integration gaps
hypotheses.name: Worker Split
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Test with module-aligned workers (one per module cluster) instead of layer-aligned
evidenceAgainst: 4 builders stayed in their lanes (integrity checker PASS)
evidenceFor: Backend built 11 routes but missed 4 endpoints vs Vanilla
Test builder produced 207 tests but methodology differed (behavior-focused vs DB-focused)
Frontend got 21 files but no shared/types imports detected in client code

hypotheses.description: Agents produced process artifacts (capsules/handoffs/receipts) without product benefit
hypotheses.name: Process Theater
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Add diagnostic value dimension to rubric
evidenceAgainst: Process artifacts provided audit trail (registry, lifecycle)
Anti-deception gate provided verifiable isolation proof
Diagnostic value is real but not captured in AGENT-5 rubric
evidenceFor: 4 handoff JSONs + 4 close receipts + 4 capsules = 12 process files
Gatekeeper results were also 3 additional process files
Process overhead consumed time that could have been implementation time
Evidence quality score (9/10) did not translate to product quality (80 vs 85.5)

hypotheses.description: Vanilla Codex was unexpectedly strong; benchmark underestimated current capability
hypotheses.name: Vanilla Strength
hypotheses.nextTestNeeded: Test at scale where Vanilla context window becomes limiting factor
evidenceAgainst: Vanilla missed source file floor (78/80) and export floor (168/300)
Vanilla had 27 test files but only 66 tests (v0.5 had 207)
evidenceFor: Vanilla achieved 85.5 with zero overhead, 40/40 endpoints, 168 exports
Vanilla produced 5 services vs v0.4's 3 (more complete)
Vanilla code was readable (v0.4 was compressed/minified)
Vanilla did not simplify the benchmark—implemented all core features

hypotheses.description: 7-agent company shape (orchestrator + 4 builders + 3 gatekeepers) is wrong for this scale
hypotheses.name: Multi-Agent Form
evidenceAgainst: 7-agent model proved worker isolation is possible with fork_context:false
Agent Company runtime infrastructure (registry, lifecycle, spawn) worked correctly
evidenceFor: 7 agents for a 13-module project is architecturally heavy
Builder split by layer (DB/Backend/Frontend/Tests) doesn't match how Codex thinks
Gatekeepers added verification value but builders needed more integration
Single builder + reviewer + verifier might achieve same quality with less overhead

rootCauseVerdict.summary: v0.5 failed to beat Vanilla primarily because: (1) OpsFlow Lite is below the complexity threshold where multi-agent adds value, (2) current Codex handles this scale efficiently in a single pass, (3) 7-agent form adds 3-4x overhead without compensating quality improvement. Orchestrator's failure to enforce floors and Reviewer's permissive closure compounded the gap.
